name: incognito-persists-nothing
description:
an incognito window must write no tab row to the persisted document.

Incognito is a PROFILE property, not a browser type, so an incognito window is is_type_normal and the bootstrap gives it an AtriumBrowserWindow and a BrowserController like any other. AddTab passes -1 for the space index, so its rows landed in whichever NON-incognito space was active, drew there, and survived into spaces.json, its .bak, its .pre-rust and the 30-day archive.

Asserted as a PRESENCE - the guard fired on a real incognito navigation - rather than as the absence of a write. An absence assertion passes just as well when the window never opened or the navigation never happened, which is the trap both earlier scenarios were built out of.

A browsertest cannot cover this: CreateIncognitoBrowser dies in browser_compositor_view_mac.mm on a GetCompositor check, which is a harness limit, not the product - Cmd+Shift+N in the VM opens a second window and the app stays up.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
SETUP: an incognito window. It is is_type_normal, so it gets a controller like any other
let the private window come up and take focus
a tab in it, which is what would have been persisted

assertions.note: Two windows, so the incognito one really opened. Without this the vlog below could be absent for the boring reason.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: tab [0-9]+ not persisted, window is off the record
assertions.note: THE CLAIM, as a presence: the write path refused a real incognito tab. The line deliberately carries no url and no title, since not recording those is the point.
